title: A Transient Alkaline Shift Reversibly Increases Association of the Chaperone ChpA with Heat-Damaged Lysozyme
authors: Elias Orin and Priya Daro | Center for Synthetic Stress Biology
research_question: Does a transient alkaline shift reversibly increase ChpA binding to heat-damaged lysozyme?
key_findings: Binding returned to 1.1-fold after 20 min at pH 7.2
Total ChpA changed by less than 6%
conclusion: The alkaline shift caused a reversible increase in ChpA binding capacity without changing abundance.
critical_negations: Total ChpA did not materially increase
